newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PacDun sees first half much lower.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PacDun sees first half much lower.

text.p: Diversified manufacturere Pacific Dunlop Ltd said on Thursday it expected the profit for the six months to December 31, 1996 to be well below the level recorded a year ago.

"...While we are forecasting an improvement in results for this financial year, the first six months will be well below the comparative period last year," Pacific Dunlop said in reply to a query over its Australian Stock Exchange (ASX).

"Trading conditions in both the manufacturing and retail industries in which we have a significant interest remain subdued, and will continue to have an impact on our results," the diversified manufacturer said.
Pacific Dunlop reported a net profit after abnormal items of A$116.64 million in the six months ended December 31, 1995.
Pacific Dunlop said there was still uncertainty surrounding the litigation of the Telectronics Pacing Systems business sold earlier this year to St Jude Medical Inc.
Although Pacific Dunlop sold Teletronics, it still retains responsibility for products manufactured prior to the sale.

"There is still too much uncertainty surrounding the scope of the litigation and its outcome for the directors of the relevant companies to responsibly make any provision with respect to liability - if indeed any exists," it said.
Pacific Dunlop shares closed eight cents higher to A$3.04 on Wednesday. The ASX queried Pacific Dunlop over its share price rise to A$3.04 from A$2.75 on December 13.
